standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: example-degree-simple-algebraic-extension (a root of an irreducible polynomial of degree d gives the extension k[x]/(P) of degree d, so an irreducible of degree > 1 yields a nontrivial finite algebraic extension); division with remainder in F[x]
core_obligations: (1) implies (2): an irreducible of degree > 1 would generate a nontrivial finite (hence algebraic) extension by the simple-extension example
(2) implies (3): an irreducible polynomial with a root is linear, so every nonconstant polynomial has a root
(3) implies (4): division with remainder factors out one root at a time and induction on the degree writes any nonconstant polynomial as c times a product of linear factors
(4) implies (1): if every polynomial is a product of linear factors, the only irreducibles are linear, so every simple subextension F(alpha)/F of an algebraic E/F is trivial, whence E = F
proof_roadmap: Use the simple-extension example for the first implication and induction for the third
